items.title: Aragón regularization: resolutions slow, Social Security registrations rise
items.body: Only a trickle of definitive resolutions has reached immigrants in Aragón after the three-month validation window closed. Nationally, 1.174.978 applications were filed between April 16 and June 30; 33.865 of them in Aragón. At the same time, foreign worker affiliation in Aragón rose over the summer, with the biggest increase in Social Security registrations since late April.

items.title: Housing anger floods Madrid as Congress rejects decrees, splits PSOE
items.body: Congress rejected two government housing decrees on Friday; between 70.000 and 500.000 people protested in central Madrid on Saturday, with demonstrations in more than 50 cities. Young renters said rent can take up to 70% of their salary. PSOE is divided over early elections, and Sánchez warned Junts, PP and Vox that history will judge them.

items.title: Pensions to rise 3,6% in January, third-largest since 2010
items.body: Pensions will be revalued by 3,6% in January, the third-largest increase since 2010. Rising fuel, gas and electricity prices are pushing inflation back up after Spain had moved closer to the 2% target recommended by central banks. The revaluation forces Social Security to make a record payout.

items.title: Small print of gas tariff cut: "Doesn't really reduce cost"
items.body: The regulated gas tariff (TUR) rose by an average of 17,6% from October 1, and part of that increase is deferred, not cancelled. RDL 25/2026 caps the raw material cost increase at 35%, giving 3,5 cents per kWh, and from January 1, 2027, the cap on increases cannot exceed 15%. OCU warns that the measure is a deferral and that the cost will be recovered in future tariff revisions.

items.title: Feijóo advances PP reform to let mutuas issue sick-leave discharges
items.body: Alberto Núñez Feijóo proposed reforms that would allow mutuas (employer mutual insurers) to issue sick-leave discharges for certain pathologies and run diagnostic tests. Sick leave is currently managed by the public health system, a red line in Spain. The proposal is part of PP's labor agenda responding to business demands, and Feijóo has previously floated cutting sick-leave pay and benefits.

items.title: ⚠️ Catalonia confines 20 comarcas under red alert as storm hits
items.body: President Salvador Illa urged people not to travel as Catalonia confined around 20 comarcas under red alert from 20:00 Saturday to 14:00 Sunday. Rodalies de Catalunya suspended almost all lines and FGC cancelled all services. Meteocat forecasts more than 200 liters per square meter along the Tarragona and Barcelona coast.

items.title: Judeline becomes first Spanish singer to top Spotify chart
items.body: Lara Fernández Castrelo, 23, known as Judeline, is the first Spanish singer to reach number 1 on Spotify's Top 50. Her single "BbY WOW" features Karol G and Rusowsky. She also sings and plays a small role in "La bola negra", the film by Los Javis representing Spain at the Oscars.

items.title: Rental crisis pushes young people into homes without living rooms
items.body: Young renters in Spain increasingly live in flats where living rooms and common areas have been turned into bedrooms. Alba, 20, pays about 360 euros a month for a room in a Málaga flat with four rented bedrooms and one bathroom, though it originally had three bedrooms. Landlords may legally convert spaces if municipal habitability conditions are met.

items.title: Majority of PP, Vox and Junts voters back anti-eviction shield
items.body: A poll shows 70% of citizens overall support protecting vulnerable people without housing alternatives from evictions. Support reaches 55% among PP voters, 53% among Vox voters and 70% among Junts voters, while 85% of PSOE voters and 86% of Sumar voters back the measure. Junts voters also support extending leases expiring before 2028; the poll was conducted by Ateneo del Dato for El Diario.

items.title: José Andrés and Jeff Bezos join Spain's housing debate
items.body: Chef José Andrés said Spain's problem is a lack of housing, not a lack of decrees, calling the government's proposals "propaganda campaigns" and "patches". He argued that subsidizing demand without increasing supply pressures prices. Jeff Bezos agreed with the diagnosis "100%" after the legislative failure of two emergency housing decrees.

items.title: CEOE calls housing general strike "illegal"
items.body: CEOE president Antonio Garamendi said a general strike over housing is not within the law because it does not stem from a labor conflict. He said he agrees there is a real housing crisis, but warned that there would be a reaction if a strike were called, and that it would affect business activity. He spoke at the Foro La Toja Vínculo Atlántico in O Grove, Pontevedra.
